findings.title: Injected adapter isolation is not an operating-system sandbox
attack_path: A host injects an adapter that falsely claims offline and side-effect-free isolation.
The adapter receives a sanitized immutable case and runs arbitrary host code.
External side effects could occur outside ReplayEngine's visibility.
evidence: The engine validates and hashes adapter identity but cannot enforce host process isolation.
The default adapter is unavailable and no CLI execution command exists.
findings.recommendation: Run production adapters in an independently enforced networkless read-only sandbox.

findings.title: Version 1 excludes high-sensitivity replay inputs
attack_path: A caller attempts to register personal, confidential, secret-like, or oversized content.
The parser rejects unsupported privacy classes, secrets, and inputs above 64 KiB.
Reports expose input and evaluation hashes rather than raw content.
evidence: Only public and internal classes are accepted.
Focused tests cover secret and privacy rejection.
findings.recommendation: Implement erasure and retention policy before accepting higher-sensitivity inputs.

findings.title: Stored target and evaluator references do not execute themselves
attack_path: A caller stores crafted bounded target or evaluator text.
The engine passes it as data only to an explicitly injected adapter.
The CLI can register and report cases but cannot execute replay.
evidence: No shell, provider, network, filesystem, or model dispatch is selected from stored metadata.
Raw output is replaced by a required SHA-256.
findings.recommendation: Keep adapter selection outside persisted target references.

findings.title: Containment and authority labels prevent implicit promotion
attack_path: A caller attempts replay during containment or treats favorable metrics as a policy change.
Embedded Safe Mode guards block case and run writes.
Reports explicitly deny causal, promotion, and deployment authority.
evidence: Direct engine Safe Mode paths are tested.
Replay does not write models, skills, routers, context policy, memory, or project state.
findings.recommendation: Require separate continuous quality gates and approval for promotion.

limitations: Adapter isolation is asserted by the host rather than OS-enforced.
Caller-authored fixtures and evaluators are not authenticated ground truth.
Paired replay does not eliminate confounding, distribution shift, or leakage.
No production adapter, raw-output retention, external network, shell dispatch, promotion, release, or deployment is provided.
